coupling: The substitution commit changes internal match-data cloning so the copied-subject ownership flag is cleared only when the caller supplies a pointer different from the match data's stored subject. At that point the stored copy is not exposed by a public getter, so the stricter branch is not reachable by an in-contract application. The later get-subject commit exposes that library-owned copied subject pointer through the public API. Once an application retrieves it and resumes substitution with PCRE2_SUBSTITUTE_MATCHED, the internal clone retains the ownership flag; freeing the internal match-data block releases the subject, after which the application's original match-data block releases it again. A correct fix has to reconcile the clone's ownership transfer with the getter's subject-lifetime contract across both commits; changing only one side leaves an API/lifetime invariant that the other edited commit relies upon.
